title: Unit 4: Reproduction
description: Comprehensive questions covering Grade 9 Biology Unit 4

questions.question: What is reproduction?
options: The ability of organisms to produce offspring of their own kind
The process of obtaining energy from food
The movement of organisms from one place to another
The response of organisms to stimuli
questions.correctAnswer: The ability of organisms to produce offspring of their own kind
questions.explanation: Reproduction is the biological process by which organisms produce offspring of their own kind, ensuring continuation of life from generation to generation.

questions.question: Which characteristic best distinguishes living things from non-living matter?
questions.explanation: The ability of organisms to reproduce to form their own kind is the one characteristic that best distinguishes living things from non-living matter.

questions.question: How many parents are involved in asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: In asexual reproduction, there is only one parent and no special reproductive organs or cells are involved.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: The basic forms of asexual reproduction are fission (binary and multiple), budding, and fragmentation.

questions.question: In which type of organism is binary fission commonly observed?
questions.explanation: Binary fission is common among bacteria, algae, and protozoa. In bacteria, the cell simply divides into two and each new cell becomes an independent organism.

questions.question: What happens to the bacterial nucleus before binary fission?
options: It is replicated to produce two identical copies
questions.correctAnswer: It is replicated to produce two identical copies
questions.explanation: Before a bacterium divides, the bacterial nucleus is replicated to produce two identical copies so that each daughter cell receives one copy.

questions.question: What is multiple fission?
options: The organism divides into more than two equal parts
The organism divides into two equal parts
The organism divides into two unequal parts
The organism does not divide at all
questions.correctAnswer: The organism divides into more than two equal parts
questions.explanation: In multiple fission, the organism divides into more than two equal parts, common among some parasitic protozoa such as malarial parasites.

questions.question: What is fragmentation in asexual reproduction?
options: Breakdown of a parent organism into parts that develop into whole organisms
Division of a cell into two equal halves
Formation of a bud on the parent body
Growth of a new plant from a seed
questions.correctAnswer: Breakdown of a parent organism into parts that develop into whole organisms
questions.explanation: Fragmentation is a mode of asexual reproduction involving the breakdown of a parent organism into parts that develop into whole organisms, observed in fungi, plants, animals, and algae.

questions.question: Which organism is given as an example of fragmentation?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra, the filamentous green-algae, undergoes fragmentation which results in many filaments, each growing into a matured filament.

questions.question: In budding, the two daughter cells are:
questions.explanation: In budding, the two daughter cells are unequal. A bulge forms on the side of the cell, the nucleus divides mitotically, and the bud detaches from the mother cell.

questions.question: Which organism reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: Yeast is a fungus that reproduces by budding. A bud develops on the surface of the yeast cell, and the nucleus divides; one daughter nucleus migrates into the bud.

questions.question: Which invertebrate animal reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: Budding occurs commonly in some invertebrate animals such as hydra, where a bud forms on the parent body and eventually detaches to become a new individual.

questions.question: What is the main form of asexual reproduction in the majority of fungi?
questions.explanation: The majority of fungi reproduce asexually by the formation of spores, a process called sporulation. Spores are dispersed by air currents and grow new hyphae.

questions.question: What is a stolon (runner) in plants?
options: A horizontal stem that grows along the surface of the soil
A modified stem that stores starch
A modified leaf that stores food
questions.correctAnswer: A horizontal stem that grows along the surface of the soil
questions.explanation: Runners (stolons) originate from auxiliary buds in the lower portion of a plant and grow along the surface of the soil. The strawberry plant is an example.

questions.question: What is a rhizome?
options: A stem that grows above the ground
A modified root that stores food
A fleshy leaf that stores nutrients
questions.explanation: Rhizomes are horizontal shoots that arise from lateral buds near the stem base and grow under the ground. Couch grass is a good example.

questions.question: Tubers are modified stems that store which substance?
questions.explanation: Tubers are modified stems that may store starch, as seen in the potato. They arise as swollen ends of stolons and contain many buds.

questions.question: Which of the following is a natural method of vegetative propagation?
questions.explanation: Bulbs are natural vegetative propagation structures. A bulb is a modified stem with enlarged fleshy leaves that functions as an underground storage unit.

questions.question: In grafting, what is the stem of the plant to be grafted called?
questions.explanation: In grafting, the stem of the plant to be grafted is known as the scion, while the root is called the stock.

questions.question: In grafting, what is the root portion called?
questions.explanation: In grafting, the root is called the stock, while the stem of the plant to be grafted is known as the scion.

questions.question: What is parthenogenesis?
options: Development of an unfertilized egg into an adult organism
Division of an organism into two equal parts
Growth of a new plant from a cutting
questions.correctAnswer: Development of an unfertilized egg into an adult organism
questions.explanation: Parthenogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction in which an unfertilized egg develops into an adult organism. In honeybees, all males (drones) are derived through parthenogenesis.

questions.question: In honeybees, bees derived through parthenogenesis are:
questions.explanation: Among honeybees, all the bees derived through parthenogenesis are males (drones). The queen bee can lay unfertilized eggs that develop into male bees.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of asexual reproduction?
options: Offspring can adapt to changing environments
questions.explanation: Advantages of asexual reproduction include: no mate is needed, no gametes are needed, and all good characteristics of the parent are passed on to the offspring.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: A disadvantage of asexual reproduction is that little variation is created, so adaptation to a changing environment (evolution) is unlikely.

questions.question: What are the sex cells called in sexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: Sex cells are called gametes. They are made in reproductive organs and are produced through meiosis. The male gamete is sperm and the female gamete is egg.

questions.question: Through which type of cell division are gametes produced?
questions.explanation: Gametes are produced through meiosis, a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, producing four genetically distinct cells.

questions.question: What is formed when a sperm and an egg unite during fertilization?
questions.explanation: Fertilization results in the formation of a single cell called a zygote. The zygote then grows into a new individual.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary sexual characteristic in males?
questions.explanation: Primary sexual characteristics are present at birth. Males are born with the penis, scrotum, and testicles. Deepening of voice and facial hair are secondary sexual characteristics.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary sexual characteristic in females?
questions.explanation: Females are born with the vagina, uterus, and ovaries. These are primary sexual characteristics. Breast development, broadening of hips, and menstruation are secondary sexual characteristics.

questions.question: What hormone is responsible for male secondary sexual characteristics?
questions.explanation: Testosterone, produced by the testes, is responsible for the growth and development of secondary sex characteristics in males, such as deepening of voice and facial hair.

questions.question: Which hormone is responsible for female secondary sexual characteristics?
questions.explanation: Estrogen, released from the ovary, is responsible for the secondary sex characteristics of females, such as breast development, broadening of hips, and fat distribution.

questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary sexual characteristic in males?
questions.explanation: Secondary sexual characteristics in males include deepening of the voice, increase in body hair, increase in muscle mass, and increased growth of long bones.

questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary sexual characteristic in females?
questions.explanation: Secondary sexual characteristics in females include broadening of the hips, fat deposited in breasts, increased growth of long bones, and the beginning of the menstrual cycle.

questions.question: What is the site of sperm production in males?
questions.explanation: Paired testes are the sites of sperm production. Each testis is composed of numerous seminiferous tubules in which sperm develop.

questions.question: Where does sperm maturation occur?
questions.explanation: Sperm travel from the seminiferous tubules to the epididymis, where sperm maturation occurs. The mature sperm then move to the vas deferens.

questions.question: What is the function of the vas deferens?
options: To convey mature sperm toward the body surface
questions.correctAnswer: To convey mature sperm toward the body surface
questions.explanation: The vas deferens is one of a pair of long ducts that convey mature sperm toward the body surface. It joins the urethra.

questions.question: What do the seminal vesicles secrete?
questions.explanation: Seminal vesicles are exocrine glands that secrete fructose-rich fluid into the vasa deferentia, providing nutrients for sperm.

questions.question: What is the function of the prostate gland?
options: To produce alkaline secretions that raise pH of the female reproductive tract
questions.correctAnswer: To produce alkaline secretions that raise pH of the female reproductive tract
questions.explanation: The prostate gland produces alkaline secretions that help raise the pH of the female reproductive tract, making it more hospitable to sperm.

questions.question: Why are the testes housed in the scrotum?
options: To provide a slightly lower temperature for viable sperm formation
To protect them from physical injury
To increase blood flow to the testes
questions.correctAnswer: To provide a slightly lower temperature for viable sperm formation
questions.explanation: The scrotum houses the testes outside the abdominal cavity to provide an environment of slightly lower temperature, since viable sperm do not form at body temperature.

questions.question: What is semen composed of?
options: Sperm mixed with secretions from seminal vesicles and prostate gland
questions.correctAnswer: Sperm mixed with secretions from seminal vesicles and prostate gland
questions.explanation: Semen is a mix of sperm, proteins, nutrients, ions, and signalling molecules. Sperm constitute less than 5 percent of semen volume.

questions.question: What is the female gonad called?
questions.explanation: The female gonads are the ovaries. They lie deep inside the pelvic cavity and produce and release eggs. They also secrete estrogens and progesterone.

questions.question: Which structure connects the ovary to the uterus?
questions.explanation: Adjacent to each ovary is an oviduct, a hollow tube that connects the ovary to the uterus. Both oviducts open onto the uterus.

questions.question: What is the function of the uterus?
options: To serve as the birth canal
questions.explanation: The uterus (womb) is specialized for housing the embryo during its intrauterine existence. It has thick muscular walls and a specialized lining called the endometrium.

questions.question: What is the narrowed region at the bottom of the uterus called?
questions.explanation: The bottom of the uterus is a narrowed region called the cervix, which opens into the vagina.

questions.question: What happens during ovulation?
options: An egg is released from the ovary into the oviduct
questions.correctAnswer: An egg is released from the ovary into the oviduct
questions.explanation: During ovulation, the follicle wall ruptures and the egg along with surrounding follicle cells is ejected into the adjacent oviduct.

questions.question: What structure develops from the ruptured follicle after ovulation?
questions.explanation: After ovulation, cells of the ruptured follicle develop into a hormone-secreting structure called the corpus luteum.

questions.question: What is the first day of the menstrual cycle marked by?
questions.explanation: The first day of the menstrual cycle is marked by the onset of menstruation (flow phase), which is the flow of bits of uterine lining and some blood.

questions.question: Which hormone stimulates the maturation of an ovarian follicle?
questions.explanation: FSH stimulates the development of follicles in the ovary, which in turn causes estrogen to be released.

questions.question: Which hormone triggers ovulation?
questions.explanation: The flow of LH (luteinizing hormone) causes the follicle to swell and burst. LH is the trigger for ovulation.

questions.question: What hormones are secreted by the corpus luteum?
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum secretes some estrogens and a lot of progesterone. These hormones cause the uterine lining to thicken in preparation for pregnancy.

questions.question: What is the process called when the fertilized egg sinks into the lining of the uterus?
questions.explanation: Implantation is the process by which the early embryo sinks into the lining of the uterus to continue its development.

questions.question: After how many weeks is the embryo called a fetus?
questions.explanation: After 8 weeks, when all the organs are formed, the embryo is called a fetus.

questions.question: What is the function of the placenta?
options: To provide oxygen and nutrients from the mother's blood to the embryo
questions.correctAnswer: To provide oxygen and nutrients from the mother's blood to the embryo
questions.explanation: The placenta provides oxygen and nutrients such as glucose and amino acids from the mother's blood to the embryo's bloodstream via the umbilical cord.

questions.question: The fluid-filled sac that protects the embryo is called:
questions.explanation: Inside the uterus, the embryo becomes enclosed in a fluid-filled sac called the amnion or water sac, which protects it from damage.

questions.question: What is the fluid inside the amnion called?
questions.explanation: The fluid inside the amnion is called amniotic fluid, which protects the embryo from damage and prevents unequal pressures from acting on it.

questions.question: Identical (monozygotic) twins come from:
options: Two eggs fertilized by two sperm
One egg fertilized by two sperm
questions.explanation: Identical (monozygotic) twins come from one zygote that splits into two. They are strikingly alike and always of the same sex.

questions.question: What is a barrier method of birth control?
questions.explanation: Condoms are barrier methods that physically prevent sperm from reaching the egg. They also provide protection against STIs.

questions.question: Which method of birth control permanently prevents gamete production or release?
questions.explanation: Sterilization is the permanent prevention of gamete production or release, achieved through tubal ligation in women or vasectomy in men.

questions.question: What is a vasectomy?
options: Cutting and sealing the vas deferens to prevent sperm from entering the urethra
Insertion of a device into the uterus
questions.correctAnswer: Cutting and sealing the vas deferens to prevent sperm from entering the urethra
questions.explanation: Vasectomy is a surgical operation in which the man's sperm ducts (vas deferens) are cut and the ends sealed, so semen contains no sperm.

questions.question: What is tubal ligation?
options: Sealing shut or tying off a section of each oviduct
Inserting a coil into the uterus
questions.correctAnswer: Sealing shut or tying off a section of each oviduct
questions.explanation: Tubal ligation is the sealing shut or tying off of a section of each oviduct to prevent eggs from traveling into the uterus.

questions.question: What does the contraceptive pill contain?
options: Chemicals similar to estrogen and progesterone
questions.correctAnswer: Chemicals similar to estrogen and progesterone
questions.explanation: The pill contains chemicals that have the same effect on the body as the hormones estrogen and progesterone, which suppress ovulation.

questions.question: How does an IUD (intra-uterine device) prevent pregnancy?
options: It prevents implantation of a fertilized ovum
questions.correctAnswer: It prevents implantation of a fertilized ovum
questions.explanation: An IUD is inserted into the wall of the uterus where it probably prevents implantation of a fertilized ovum. It is about 98% effective.

questions.question: What is the most effective natural method of preventing pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Abstinence involves a couple avoiding sexual intercourse. It is the most effective method with the added advantage of preventing exposure to sexually transmitted pathogens.

questions.question: Which of the following STIs is caused by the flagellated protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis?
questions.explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by the flagellated protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis. Symptoms include yellowish discharge and sore, itchy vagina in some infected women.

questions.question: Which STI is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis?
questions.explanation: Chlamydia is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis, which are small bacteria. Left untreated, it can scar the reproductive tract and lead to infertility.

questions.question: Which bacterium causes gonorrhea?
questions.explanation: Gonorrhea is caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Symptoms in men include yellow pus from the penis and painful urination.

questions.question: Which STI is caused by Treponema pallidum?
questions.explanation: Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum, a spiral-shaped bacterium. If untreated, it can damage the liver, bones, and eventually the brain.

questions.question: What does HIV stand for?
questions.explanation: HIV stands for Human Immunodeficiency Virus. It kills immune cells in the body and leads to Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS).

questions.question: How is HIV primarily transmitted?
options: Through blood or body fluids of an infected person
questions.correctAnswer: Through blood or body fluids of an infected person
questions.explanation: HIV is spread from an infected person through blood or body fluids, including intimate sexual contact, contaminated needles, blood transfusion, and from mother to fetus.

questions.question: Which of the following STIs is bacterial and can be treated with antibiotics?
questions.explanation: Syphilis is caused by a bacterium (Treponema pallidum) and can be treated with antibiotics if recognized early. Viral STIs like HIV cannot be cured with antibiotics.

questions.question: Which of the following is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: HIV/AIDS is caused by a virus. Unlike bacterial STIs, antibiotics are not effective against viral STIs.

questions.question: Which of the following STIs can be passed from mother to child during birth, causing pneumonia and conjunctivitis in the newborn?
questions.explanation: Chlamydia infection can be passed from mother to child during birth, causing pneumonia and conjunctivitis in the newborn. It can be cured with antibiotics.

questions.question: What does AIDS stand for?
questions.explanation: AIDS stands for Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome and is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).

questions.question: Early symptoms of AIDS may include:
options: Swollen lymph nodes, weight loss, fever, and fatigue
questions.correctAnswer: Swollen lymph nodes, weight loss, fever, and fatigue
questions.explanation: Early symptoms of AIDS include swollen lymph nodes, loss of appetite, weight loss, fever, rashes, night sweats, and fatigue.

questions.question: Spermicides work by:
questions.explanation: Spermicides are chemicals that kill or immobilize sperm. They are placed in the vagina and are more effective when used with condoms or diaphragms.

questions.question: Which naturally occurring method of vegetative propagation involves horizontal stems that grow under the ground?
questions.explanation: Rhizomes are horizontal shoots that arise from lateral buds and grow under the ground. Couch grass is a good example.

questions.question: Corms are similar to rhizomes but are more:
questions.explanation: Corms are similar to rhizomes but are more rounded and fleshy (such as in gladiolus). They contain stored food that enables some plants to survive winter.

questions.question: What is the function of the bulbourethral glands?
options: To secrete lubricating mucus into the urethra
questions.correctAnswer: To secrete lubricating mucus into the urethra
questions.explanation: Bulbourethral glands secrete a lubricating mucus into the urethra, which helps clear the urethra of residual urine before ejaculation.

questions.question: What type of cell division produces two identical daughter cells in asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: In binary fission, the body of the unicellular parent divides by mitosis into two approximately equal parts, each growing into an individual similar to the parent.

questions.question: What is the ribbed lining of the uterus called?
questions.explanation: The uterus has a specialized lining called the endometrium, which consists of glandular epithelium, connective tissues, and blood vessels.

questions.question: What is the withdrawal method of contraception?
options: The man pulls his penis out of the vagina before ejaculation
The woman takes a pill after intercourse
A condom is used during intercourse
An IUD is inserted into the uterus
questions.correctAnswer: The man pulls his penis out of the vagina before ejaculation
questions.explanation: The withdrawal method involves a man pulling his penis out of his partner's vagina before ejaculation to prevent sperm from entering the vagina.

questions.question: During the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle, what does LH stimulate?
questions.explanation: During the luteal phase, LH stimulates formation of the corpus luteum, which secretes estrogens and progesterone to thicken the uterine lining.

questions.question: The sperm contains many mitochondria in its midpiece for:
options: Producing enzymes to penetrate the egg
questions.explanation: The midsection of a sperm contains many mitochondria that supply the energy required for flagellar movement to swim toward the egg.

questions.question: The head of a sperm contains enzymes that help:
questions.explanation: The sperm head is covered by enzymes that help the sperm penetrate an egg during fertilization.
